subject: Analysing recombinant, clonal and migrant population using DArT markers in haploid fungi

messages.author: d89993b905b0ab8c
messages.subject: Analysing recombinant, clonal and migrant population using DArT markers in haploid fungi
parts:
Hi there, 

I am trying to analysis DArT markers, which is a dominant marker (presence/absence only) to find out recombinant, a clonal and migrant population in a field trial in haploid fungi. Planning on using bitwise distance (Provesti’s distance). Could you please point me to the appropriate document, which talks about the haploid and dominant marker analysis (Most of the documents are on codominant markers and diploid population) And also, bitwise distance only handle SNP data or can I use it for the dominant marker as well? Any help would be appreciated. 

Thanks, 
Barsha

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Analysing recombinant, clonal and migrant population using DArT markers in haploid fungi
parts:
Hi Barsha,

We cover genetic distances in our recent review (See Box 2 of http://apsjournals.apsnet.org/doi/abs/10.1094/PHYTO-12-16-0425-RVW).

In short, Prevosti's distance (aka simple mismatch, aka manhattan... there are MANY names for this distance) will give you the fraction of alleles at which two individuals differ. In the case of dominant markers, this is also the fraction of loci. Regardless of marker type, it also has the nice property of being equivalent to the squared Euclidean distance for haploids.

I've mentioned this before on this forum and in the documentation, but bitwise.dist() is for genlight objects. It will work with genind objects, but in the background it's just calling prevosti.dist() [1]. There are three functions that all do the same thing in poppr (diss.dist(), prevosti.dist(), and bitwise.dist()) [2, 3], and the only one that's truly different is bitwise.dist because it's optimized for data that's been coded as bits.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

[1]: http://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/bitwise.dist.html#note
[2]: http://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/diss.dist.html#note
[3]: http://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/genetic_distance.html#note

messages.author: d4586792679cf1d0
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Analysing recombinant, clonal and migrant population using DArT markers in haploid fungi
parts:
Hi Barsha,

Think of your data as being haploid. Analysis is straightforward for haploid (viral, bacterial or fungal) organisms based on allele frequencies. you cannot do Fst, but you can do most of everything else that is based on population allele frequencies.

Best wishes,
Nik
